## Answer Key: Chapter 4 {#sec-solutions-ch4 .unnumbered}

Full solutions to Chapter 4's "Check your understanding" questions
(@sec-ch4-check).

**1. Structural identification. In ZeRO-3 (equivalently, FSDP), which
of the following are sharded across the data-parallel group: optimizer
states, gradients, parameters, activations?**

*Answer.* Optimizer states, gradients, and parameters are all sharded
across the data-parallel group in ZeRO-3 ($P_{os+g+p}$). Activations
are *not* sharded by ZeRO — each DP replica processes a different
micro-batch, so its activations already differ from every other
replica's and are never duplicated in the first place, so there is
nothing to shard there.

*Common trap:* Assuming ZeRO shards "everything," including
activations, rather than specifically the three model-state objects
(optimizer states, gradients, parameters) that vanilla DP would
otherwise replicate identically on every rank.

**2. Calculation. A cluster has 32 devices. You set tp=4 and pp=2,
with no context or expert parallelism. What data-parallel degree is
implied, and how many devices form one complete model replica?**

*Answer.* $\text{dp} = 32 / (4 \times 2) = 4$. One complete model
replica uses $\text{tp} \times \text{pp} = 4 \times 2 = 8$ devices
(with cp and ep both implicitly 1).

*Common trap:* Dividing the world size by only one of tp or pp instead
of their product, or forgetting that the axes not explicitly set (cp,
ep) still act as factors of 1 in the world-size factorization.

**3. Calculation. With a micro-batch size of 3, 4 gradient-accumulation
steps, and a data-parallel degree of 8, what is the global batch
size?**

*Answer.* $\text{gbs} = 3 \times 4 \times 8 = 96$.

*Common trap:* Omitting the data-parallel multiplier and reporting
only the per-replica local batch ($3 \times 4 = 12$) as if it were the
global batch size.

**4. Misconception check. True or false: increasing the
pipeline-parallelism degree is mathematically equivalent to increasing
the data-parallel degree, since both let you use more GPUs for
training.**

*Answer.* False. Increasing the DP degree adds more identical, full
model replicas, each processing different data, synchronized by
gradient all-reduce. Increasing the PP degree instead splits the
*same* model into more, smaller stages, each holding *different*
layers and passing activations point-to-point to its neighbor — no
stage in a PP setup holds a full model replica, unlike every rank in a
DP setup.

*Common trap:* Treating "more GPUs used" as the defining property of a
parallelism strategy, rather than looking at what is actually
replicated versus sharded and what is actually communicated.

**5. Interview/design. You must train a model on 64 devices. A single
layer's weights and activations require a tensor-parallelism degree
of exactly 8 to fit in one device's memory (consistent with its
key/value head count, which also permits at most tp=8), and its
optimizer states and gradients require a data-parallel group of at
least 8 devices to fit in memory even after full ZeRO/FSDP sharding.
Propose one parallelism combination (state a degree for each axis you
use) that satisfies both requirements and multiplies out to exactly
64 devices, and justify your choice in one or two sentences.**

*Answer.* $\text{tp}=8$, $\text{dp}=8$, $\text{pp}=1$, $\text{cp}=1$,
$\text{ep}=1$ (product $= 64$). Justification: the per-layer memory
requirement fixes $\text{tp}=8$ exactly (not merely "at most 8"); with
tp already fixed, the remaining factor of $64/8=8$ must be distributed
among dp, pp, cp, and ep, and since $\text{dp}\ge 8$ is separately
required for optimizer-state/gradient memory, the only way to satisfy
both stated requirements at once is $\text{dp}=8$ with
$\text{pp}=\text{cp}=\text{ep}=1$. TP addresses per-layer
weight/activation residency; the size of the data-parallel (and
therefore ZeRO/FSDP-shardable) group addresses the separate
optimizer-state/gradient memory problem — these are two distinct
memory problems solved by two different axes. Given both stated
requirements, this is the *only* valid combination: any other
$(\text{tp},\text{dp},\text{pp},\text{cp},\text{ep})$ tuple that
multiplies to 64 either sets $\text{tp}\ne 8$ (violating the per-layer
requirement) or sets $\text{dp}<8$ (violating the optimizer-state/
gradient requirement).

*Common trap:* Proposing a combination whose degrees do not multiply
to 64, proposing $\text{tp}\ne 8$ (violating the stated per-layer
memory/K-V-head requirement), or proposing $\text{dp}<8$ (violating
the stated optimizer-state/gradient memory requirement). It is also a
mistake to describe $\text{dp}=8$ as merely one choice that
"maximizes" the data-parallel group among several options, rather than
recognizing that the two stated requirements force it to be exactly 8.
